title: Long-term Prognostic Value of Sequential Coronary CT Angiography and Quantitative PET in Suspected Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Multicentre study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The long-term prognostic value of a guideline-recommended selective sequential anatomical-functional imaging strategy using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) followed by quantitative [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) remains uncertain. We evaluated its long-term prognostic value in patients with first symptoms suggestive of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). METHODS: In this multicentre European cohort, symptomatic patients first underwent CCTA and were selectively referred to quantitative [15O]H2O PET in case of suspected obstructive stenosis (≥50%). Patients were stratified according to CCTA findings and PET-derived ischaemia (normal CCTA; non-obstructive CAD on CCTA; obstructive CAD on CCTA without ischaemia; obstructive CAD on CCTA with ischaemia). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for unstable angina (UA). Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated. RESULTS: Among 3,918 patients (61.0±9.8 years; 54.3% female) with a median follow-up of 5.1 [3.8-8.0] years, 278 (7.1%) experienced the primary endpoint. aHRs increased stepwise across CCTA-PET categories. Compared to normal CCTA, non-obstructive CAD and obstructive CAD without ischaemia were associated with a higher risk of the combined primary endpoint (aHR 1.89, [95%CI: 1.23-2.91], p=0.004; aHR 3.20, [95%CI: 1.95-5.25], p<0.001). Among patients with obstructive CAD on CCTA, PET-derived ischaemia further increased the risk of the primary endpoint (aHR 1.55, [95%CI: 1.05-2.30]; p=0.029), but not when excluding UA from the composite endpoint (aHR 1.37, [95%CI 0.90-2.07]; p=0.141). PET-derived ischaemia primarily predicted events within the first year, while obstructive CCTA findings remained associated with long-term hard outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: A sequential strategy combining CCTA and quantitative [15O]H2O PET provides robust and incremental long-term risk stratification. While PET-derived ischaemia refines prediction of short-term and symptom-driven events, CCTA-derived CAD remains the principal determinant of long-term hard outcomes.

title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial.
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01-1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 .

title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The virtual circle method is currently used in preprocedural computed tomography planning for Redo-transcatheter aortic valve (TAV) replacement to simulate the predicted outer boundary of the index TAV and the valve-to-aorta distance for coronary risk assessment, yet its accuracy against postprocedural observations has not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of the virtual circle method in predicting index TAV expansion and coronary risk following a second TAV implantation using paired preprocedural and postprocedural computed tomography in patients undergoing Redo-TAV replacement. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 58 patients who underwent Redo-TAV replacement at 5 sites with paired preprocedural and postprocedural cardiac computed tomography. Three valve combinations were analyzed: Evolut-in-SAPIEN (n=17), SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN (n=13), and SAPIEN-in-Evolut (n=28). Index TAV frame expansion was quantified by area- or perimeter-derived diameter change. Accuracy of the virtual circle method was defined as a diameter difference within ±1 mm between predicted and observed index TAV frame diameter. RESULTS: In the Evolut-in-SAPIEN combination, meaningful index SAPIEN frame expansion occurred only with effective pre/postdilatation, whereas in both the SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, consistent frame expansion was observed regardless of dilatation. Changes in index frame diameter corresponded inversely to changes in valve-to-aorta distance. In the SAPIEN-in-Evolut combination, expansion was governed chiefly by implant position and sizing strategy. Across all combinations in which the virtual circle method was applicable (n=53), accurate prediction was achieved in 31 patients (58.5%), with overestimation in 14 (26.4%) and underestimation in 8 (15.1%). CONCLUSIONS: The virtual circle method provided an accurate or conservative (overestimating) estimate of index TAV expansion and coronary risk in the majority of patients (85%), supporting its clinical utility for Redo-TAVR planning. The remaining 15% showed underestimation of modest magnitude (median, 1.3 mm), occurring predominantly in patients who underwent predilatation and postdilatation, warranting heightened caution in borderline coronary anatomy when dilatation strategies are employed.

title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).

title: Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings. METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF. RESULTS: Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms. CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

title: Comprehensive m6A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure.
abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that epitranscriptomic regulation, particularly the m6A modification, contributes to heart failure progression. However, modification dynamics are not yet mapped and studied at base resolution and transcript isoform level. Here we use Nanopore direct RNA sequencing to profile m6A remodeling at transcriptome-wide and site-specific resolution in a mouse heart failure model. We identify thousands of differentially methylated sites with distinct sequence motifs and associations with RNA regulatory and cardiac function processes. Cross-species comparison reveals conserved m6A regulatory features in mouse and human heart failure. Isoform-resolved analysis further uncovers co/posttranscriptional regulation events involving isoform switching and m6A regulation in the SYNPO2L transcript. Mechanistically, m6A modification, alternative promoter usage and associated regulatory elements collectively explain this observation. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive, high-resolution characterization of m6A landscape and its remodeling in heart failure. Isoform-level regulation exemplifies an underappreciated shaping of RNA expression and modification.

title: Efficacy of fludrocortisone for symptom relief in patients with autonomic syncope and hypotensive phenotype.
abstract: AIM: To assess the efficacy of fludrocortisone therapy in patients with autonomic syncope and hypotensive phenotype. METHODS AND RESULTS: Multicentre, prospective, non-randomized study. Fludrocortisone therapy was guided by clinician experience and supported by two 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) assessments-one before treatment start (ABPM 1) and one after drug optimization (ABPM 2). Primary endpoint: reduction of the syncope burden and presyncopal symptoms based on validated semi structured questionnaires. Secondary endpoint: hypotensive episodes on ABPM. In a cohort of 94 patients treated with fludrocortisone (median age 38 [IQR 21-57]) years, 83% females), 16 patients stopped therapy due to side effects, occurring during optimization (#11) or follow-up (#5). A total of 83 patients were analysed. The average 24-hour systolic blood pressure (SBP) increased from 106.3 ± 8.2 mmHg at ABPM 1 to 112.3 ± 9.3 at ABPM 2 (p = 0.0001). The number of daytime SBP drops <90 mmHg and <100 mmHg decreased by 61%, and 45% respectively (p < 0.001 for both). The annual syncope burden was reduced by 50.2%, from 2.0 (IQR 1.0-4.0) before therapy to 0.0 (IQR 0.0-1.8) episodes during a median follow-up of 12.9 months (p = 0.0001). Subjective symptom improvement was reported by 85.6% of patients. The frequency of syncope/presyncope decreased significantly, p = 0.009. The outcome was similar in 42 younger (23 ± 6 yrs) and in 41 older (56 ± 12 yrs) patients. CONCLUSION: Fludrocortisone therapy was associated with reduced hypotension and the burden of symptoms both in younger and in older patients. Side effects lead to discontinuation of therapy in 17% of cases.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction. METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates. RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

title: Implications of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1RAs, and Nonsteroidal MRAs on the Anticipated Burden of Heart Failure.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Several treatments that reduce the risk of heart failure (HF) have been introduced recently. Their impact on the future burden of HF in the U.S. has not been well characterized. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to estimate the potential impact of recently approved cardiometabolic medications on the future burden of HF in the United States. METHODS: Using a nationally representative sample of persons in the United States 30-79 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline, we used the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equation to estimate the 10- and 30-year burden of HF and the projected impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on these estimates. The authors estimated the total number of HF cases that could be averted with risk-based treatment and calculated the number needed to treat to prevent HF. RESULTS: An estimated 5.5 million (95% CI: 5.1-5.8 million) U.S. adults 30-79 years of age without established cardiovascular disease will develop HF over 10 years. It is estimated to decrease to 5.1 million (95% CI: 4.7-5.4 million) with indicated treatment with a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, 5.2 million (95% CI: 4.8-5.6 million) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, 5.4 million (95% CI: 5.0-5.7 million) with nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and 4.8 million (95% CI: 4.4-5.2 million) with the use of combination therapy. The use of combination therapy in eligible persons with an estimated 10-year HF risk of ≥10% would result in 6.8 million (95% CI: 6.1-7.5 million) eligible participants, and 498,000 (95% CI: -663,000 to -319,000) fewer cases of HF, with a number needed to treat of 14 (95% CI: 10-22) to prevent 1 incident case. CONCLUSIONS: The projected burden of HF in the U.S. is substantial. A risk-based approach to preventive treatment may help reduce this considerably. The feasibility of such an approach deserves further investigation.

title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment. METHODS: The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome. RESULTS: Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50). CONCLUSIONS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05371496.

title: Dapagliflozin for Renal Protection in Heart Transplant Recipients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Progressive kidney disease is common in heart transplant recipients due to calcineurin inhibitor exposure and pre-existing comorbidities. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors may attenuate the decline in kidney function, but evidence in heart transplant recipients is limited. METHODS: The DAPAgliflozin for Renal protection in Heart Transplant recipients (DAPARHT) trial is a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted at six heart transplant centers in Northern Europe. We randomized adult heart transplant recipients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥25 mL/min/1.73 m² at least one year after transplantation 1:1 to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg or matching placebo once daily. The primary endpoint was the slope of the eGFR from 2 weeks after treatment initiation to the end of the 12-month blinded treatment period. RESULTS: Between June 2022 and September 2025, we randomized 430 participants, of whom 217 were allocated to dapagliflozin and 213 were allocated to placebo. We included the 424 patients with at least one eGFR measurement after baseline in the full analysis set. Their mean age was 53 ± 14 years and 29& were women. The eGFR at baseline was 67 ± 22 mL/min/1.73 m2. The median time from transplantation was 7 (3 - 13) years. Dapagliflozin improved the chronic slope of the eGFR compared with placebo. The change in the eGFR from 2 weeks to 12 months after treatment initiation was 2.0 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.0 - 3.1) mL/min/1.73 m2 in the dapagliflozin group and 0.3 (95% CI -0.8 - 1.4) mL/min/1.73 m2 in the placebo group for a between-group difference of 1.7 (95% confidence interval 0.1 - 3.3) mL/min/1.73 m²; p = 0.03. There were no unexpected safety signals and similar rates of adverse events, including infections, between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In heart transplant recipients, dapagliflozin, compared with placebo, improved the slope of the eGFR from 2 weeks to 12 months of treatment.

title: Multimodality Imaging Across the Lifespan in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
abstract: Repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) is a common condition encountered across pediatric and adult congenital heart disease clinics. Although childhood survival is excellent, patients remain at risk for late complications, including exercise intolerance, arrhythmias, heart failure, and sudden death. Residual lesions, most notably pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, drive progressive right and secondary left ventricular remodeling, often necessitating repeat interventions such as pulmonary valve replacement. Multimodality imaging is central to management, enabling risk stratification and informing the optimal timing of reintervention. This State-of-the-Art Review summarizes the current state of the art in multimodality imaging for rTOF across the lifespan, highlighting established and emerging techniques. The authors discuss the roles of 2- and 3-dimensional echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, strain and exercise imaging, ultrafast ultrasound, and advanced cardiac magnetic resonance methods in characterizing ventricular function, remodeling, mechanics, flow dynamics, fibrosis, stiffness, and electromechanical interactions. The authors explore developments in image-based machine learning and computational modeling that support patient-specific intervention planning and personalized care.

title: Local Conformal Auditing Exposes and Restores Reliability of AI-ECG Atrial Fibrillation Detection Under External Deployment Shift.
abstract: BACKGROUND: AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can detect atrial fibrillation (AF), but safe deployment depends on calibration, subgroup reliability, and explicit error guarantees, not on discrimination alone. OBJECTIVE: To test whether the conformal-prediction coverage guarantee of an AF ECG classifier survives external deployment shift, and whether a small local labeled audit restores it without retraining. METHODS: A four-class 12-lead rhythm classifier trained on PTB-XL (Germany; 7,831 ECGs, 7,164 patients) was evaluated unchanged on Chinese (Chapman-Shaoxing; n=2,289) and US (Georgia; n=1,990) cohorts. We measured discrimination, expected calibration error (ECE), 90%-target split-conformal coverage, subgroup coverage, label-free shift corrections, local recalibration across audit sizes, and an AF auto-clear policy with finite-sample risk control. RESULTS: AF AUC remained 0.998 (95% CI 0.997-0.999) in China but fell to 0.936 (0.919-0.952) in the US cohort. ECE rose from 0.051 to 0.197 and 0.237, and source-calibrated coverage fell from 0.901 to 0.758 and 0.722 (both P<0.001). Coverage was lower in Chinese men than women (0.707 vs 0.822; difference 0.115, 95% CI 0.081-0.148). Label-free corrections failed. Local recalibration restored mean coverage to 0.90 with 50 labeled ECGs but with wide variability (95% simulation interval 0.82-0.97), narrowing to 0.86-0.94 at 200 ECGs. Local AF risk control certified auto-clearing of 68% of held-out ECGs in China but abstained in the US cohort. CONCLUSION: AI-ECG uncertainty can fail silently despite high AUC. A local conformal audit detects when uncertainty estimates are untrustworthy and recalibrates the uncertainty layer without changing the classifier, converting trust into a measurable, subgroup-aware, task-specific guarantee.

title: Obesity, frail obesity, and outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation: a pooled analysis of the MOMENTUM 3 trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obesity in patients supported by left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) is linked to excess mortality and haemocompatibility-related events. Whether this association persists with the fully magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 (HM3) pump is unknown. This analysis tested outcomes with obesity and the additive influence of co-existing frailty ('frail obesity') in the contemporary era. METHODS: The study pooled 2200 HM3 recipients from the MOMENTUM 3 pivotal randomized trial (n = 515) and Continued Access Protocol (n = 1685). Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 and frailty by a 40-item Rockwood cumulative-deficit frailty index (FI), with clinically relevant frailty defined as FI ≥0.325 (moderate-severe frailty); BMI was excluded from the FI to avoid mathematical coupling. The primary endpoint was survival to transplant, recovery, or 24 months of support free of disabling stroke (modified Rankin score >3) or pump replacement reoperation. RESULTS: Obese patients (n = 887, 40.3%) were younger, less often with ischaemic aetiology, and more frequently women, but more often had diabetes and hypertension, than non-obese patients. Unadjusted 2-year outcomes were similar between groups (freedom from the primary endpoint: 75.1% vs 77.1%, log-rank P = .34; survival: 79.9% vs 81.2%, P = .57). After covariate adjustment, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.58) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.67), as well as heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia, but not stroke, bleeding, or early right heart failure. Frailty affected 67.3% of obese recipients (571/849) and was associated with a higher adjusted risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10), overall mortality and non-haemocompatibilty-related morbidity endpoints. The obesity-by-frailty interaction was not significant for either the primary endpoint (P = .436) or mortality (P = .215), indicating additive rather than synergistic risk; frail-obese patients nonetheless carried the highest absolute risk of any subgroup. Frailty improved by at least one severity class by 6 months in 75.9% of frail-obese patients, and improvement was associated with better survival (adjusted HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.26). CONCLUSIONS: In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia. Frailty was independently associated with adverse outcomes across nearly all endpoints and was highly prevalent among obese recipients; the combination of obesity and frailty was additive but not synergistic, with frail-obese patients carrying the highest absolute risk. Frailty, however, proved substantially reversible after LVAD support, and its improvement was associated with markedly better survival. Obesity and frailty should therefore be assessed together, rather than through BMI thresholds alone, with recognition that frailty status is dynamic after implantation and that improvement in frailty is associated with markedly better survival.

title: Characteristics and Mechanisms of Septal Myocardial Injury and Repair Following Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) requires screwing the lead deep into the interventricular septum. Multiple attempts are often required to achieve proper capture of the conduction system. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of deep screwing attempts on septal myocardial injury and repair and to explore the underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Prospective LBBAP implantation was performed in 41 patients with bradycardia. Serum creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) and left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (GLS) were used to evaluate myocardial damage. Mechanisms of septal damage were explored in 24 LBBAP canines using histopathological and molecular changes. RESULTS: Compared to patients with ≤ 3 attempts, those with >3 attempts had a higher incidence of CK-MB elevation (6 vs. 44%, P=0.004), a less negative LV endocardial (-17.9 vs. -13.6 %, P<0.001), and mid-myocardial GLS (-15.3 vs. -12.4 %, P<0.001). In animal study, molecular changes associated with >3 attempts featured amplified HMGB1-centered sterile inflammation and enhanced CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic remodeling. Canines with >3 attempts were characterized by three markedly thickened concentric reparative layers around the lead-inner thrombus layer, middle fibrous sheath layer, and outer reactive fibrotic layer. Interestingly, removal of the pacing lead after >3 attempts resulted in only mild scattered fibrosis, with markedly attenuated CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic pathway. CONCLUSIONS: LBBAP with >3 deep septal screwing attempts was associated with a higher risk of septal myocardial injury and markedly thickened concentric reparative layers, underpinned by more pronounced sterile inflammation, profibrotic remodeling, and foreign body reaction.

title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival. RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

title: Androgen Imbalance, Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages, and Mortality in Men.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Androgen measures reflect adiposity, metabolic health, and systemic illness, but their associations with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and mortality may differ across measures and combined profiles. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to examine associations of total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), calculated free testosterone (cFT), and joint TT-SHBG phenotypes with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome and mortality. METHODS: We analyzed men aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013 to 2016 using survey-weighted logistic (odds ratio [OR]) and Cox (hazard ratio [HR]) regression models. Advanced CKM syndrome comprised determinate National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey-adapted stages 3 to 4; cFT was calculated using the Vermeulen equation. Analyses assessed adiposity adjustment and mortality robustness. RESULTS: Among 5,505 men, 4,005 had determinate CKM status. Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome (OR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.31-2.42), but the association was attenuated after adjustment for body mass index (OR: 1.27; 95% CI: 0.90-1.79) or waist circumference (OR: 1.22; 95% CI: 0.85-1.75), suggesting that adiposity may partly account for this association. Low TT and cFT measures showed no consistent association with all-cause mortality. In exploratory analyses, the low-TT/high-SHBG phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR: 2.06; 95% CI: 1.18-3.58). CONCLUSIONS: Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome, but this association was strongly adiposity-dependent. The low-TT/high-SHBG profile showed an exploratory mortality association not observed for TT or cFT alone and may represent a distinct systemic-vulnerability phenotype. These findings underscore the noninterchangeability of androgen measures and support prospective evaluation of combined TT-SHBG profiles.

title: Normative Values for QRS Duration in Athletes aged 12-35 years undergoing Pre-participation Exams.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to limited data on athletic QRS duration, this cross-sectional study aims to establish normative digital reference values in asymptomatic, apparently healthy athletes ages 12 to 35 undergoing pre-participation examinations. OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that QRS duration of athletes would be longer in males, increase with age, and rarely exceed 120 ms in the absence of a bundle branch block. METHODS: We analyzed QRS duration from standardized digital ECG recordings in 9,084 athletes (58% male, age 12-35 years, mean age 18) obtained during pre-participation examinations. Sex-stratified 99th-percentile quantile-regression equations were developed and applied in an APP to demonstrate that QRS duration outliers could be easily identified. RESULTS: Females had shorter QRS durations than males (88.5 +/- 8.3 ms vs. 97.3 +/- 9.1 ms; mean difference 8.9 ms, 95% CI: 8.5-9.2 ms). QRS duration demonstrated a positive cross-sectional association with age and was greater in men than women. Female 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 106.0 ms and 108.0 ms, respectively, with range 62-130 ms. Male 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 116.0 ms and 118.3 ms, respectively, with range 70-132 ms. 7(0.2%) females and 55 (1.0%) males had QRS duration >120 ms. 99th percentile quantile regression equations were derived (Female: QRS=99.6 + 0.56 x age; Male: QRS = 104.7 + 0.74 x age). CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that defining prolonged QRS criteria necessitates adjustments according to age and sex. To facilitate future prospective research, we offer specific regression models to detect outliers.

title: Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B. METHODS: Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis. RESULTS: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P=0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P=0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P<0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P=0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P<0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P<0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04153149.

title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question. METHODS: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered. RESULTS: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month. CONCLUSIONS: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking. OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026. INTERVENTION: Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points. RESULTS: Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07477002.
